answer: A public atlas maps every agent identity to a single hardware-attested compute receipt: each identity must periodically solve a unique, non-parallelizable puzzle bound to its own key, and the receipt is pinned on a shared ledger. An attacker cloning identities hits a ledge — each extra identity demands another full puzzle and another attested device, so cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Identities whose receipts crumble like shale under re-verification lose their stake and their place in the atlas.
